The Membership Plugin  WordPress plugin before 4.0.6 does not verify that the membership referenced in a saved-card payment request belongs to the user making it, allowing subscriber-level members to disclose another member's Stripe payment client secret and attach a payment method of their choosing

The A2Reviews WordPress plugin through 1.2.3 does not properly verify authorization on several of its API command handlers, relying on a signature keyed on a value that is empty by default on an unconnected install, allowing unauthenticated attackers to modify A2Reviews WordPress plugin through 1.2.

The WPGraphQL WordPress plugin before 2.27.1 does not restrict access to posts in custom non-public post statuses, allowing users with the Contributor role and above to read the content of other users' posts in those statuses.

The Burst Statistics  WordPress plugin before 3.7.5 does not enforce a shared report's date range on the analytics it serves to the report's share link, allowing anyone holding the link to read the report's statistics for any period the site retains rather than the period the report was shared for.

The Custom Block Builder  WordPress plugin before 3.0.0 does not properly deny unauthorised requests to its REST routes, as its permission checks return a non-error response that WordPress treats as granted, allowing unauthenticated users to execute arbitrary PHP code on the server.

The Auth Armor  WordPress plugin through 1.0.3 does not require authentication on several handlers available to logged-out users, which leak the site's stored API credentials and allow an unauthenticated attacker to reset an administrator's enrollment and take over that administrator account.

The RegistrationMagic  WordPress plugin before 6.1.0.4 does not sanitise and escape a parameter before using it in a SQL statement, which could allow high privilege users such as admin to perform SQL injection attacks.
